title: Classic Cheese Fondue
notes: Try to keep the fondue mixture warm enough so that it stays liquid but not so hot that it burns. If you achieve this a layer will develop on the bottom of the fondue pot that has the texture of a cracker. This is called the religieuse (French for the nun) and it is a delicious way to finish the meal. Tradition states that if you lose the bread in the cheese you must buy a round of drinks for the whole party or kiss someone at the table.

ingredientSections.heading: Classic Cheese Fondue
items: 500g Cheese (see below), grated, not including any rind
1 Clove Garlic, peeled, cut in half

ingredientSections.heading: Classic Fondue
items: If you would like this blend milder, increase the Emmenthal, and decrease the Gruyere. If you would like it stronger, then do the opposite.

methodSections.heading: Classic Cheese Fondue
steps: Rub the inside surface of the fondue pot with the garlic.
In a bowl toss the grated cheese with the cornstarch.
Heat wine in a saucepan on the stove. Add a pinch of salt and pepper, and a dash of freshly grated nutmeg.
Stir in the cheese mixture gradually and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring frequently, until the mixture is thick and smooth.
Transfer to a heated fondue pot and serve with cubed bread.

methodSections.heading: Traditional Accompaniments
steps: Cubed bread. Day old is just fine, it's sturdy, and doesn't easily break up in all the gooey delicious cheese.
Cornichons, pickled onions and baby boiled potatoes.
Raw vegetables such as broccoli, cauliflower, mushrooms, or even cooked meats.
